title: Stochastic Reserve Credit Schedule and Eviction Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This sheet prototypes a stochastic, cost-aware reserve policy for multi-region GPU fleet failover. Focus: how much spare to hold by region, how to fund temporary preemptible borrowing, and an eviction+handoff checklist for regional DR events. This is intentionally conversational/worksheet style (numbers are scenarios, not final asks).

ASSUMPTIONS:
- Traffic shock model: P95 spike is +55% sustained for 30m, P99 spike +140% for 10m.
- Primary regions: us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1. Cross-region failover RTT cost ignored for capacity sizing (handled in routing policy).
- Baseline contended GPU utilization target: 68% (production).
- We allow preemptible borrow up to 12% of provisioned fleet for emergency bursts.

Scenario table (rows are independent simulations):
Region,GPUs_total,Baseline_util_pct,Target_reserve_pct,Reserved_gpus,Preemptible_ceiling,Warm_pool_min,Failover_margin_gpus
us-west1,1200,68,12,144,144,48,96
us-east1,900,66,14,126,108,36,72
eu-west1,600,65,16,96,72,24,48

Notes on columns:
- Target_reserve_pct: percent of fleet kept cold/warm to absorb regional failover without crossing 85% utilization SLA.
- Reserved_gpus = round(GPUs_total * Target_reserve_pct).
- Preemptible_ceiling: short-term borrow pool; plan is to pay spot premium and autoscale back after shock.
- Warm_pool_min: smallest hot-warm instances kept ready with DR image and KV caches primed (approx 3-5 minute spin up).
- Failover_margin_gpus: extra slack above reserved to allow staged draining and traffic shaping.

Cost tradeoff quick math (example us-west1):
- Holding 144 reserved GPUs annual amortized cost vs expected cost of on-demand borrowing during 12 P99 events/year. If average spike length 10m, borrowed hours ~20h/year. Balance at ~8-10x cost multiplier of reserved vs borrow means reserve only if frequency > X. (See linked Confluence model for exact numbers).

Eviction + Handoff Playbook (short checklist):
1) Detection: alert if region CPU/GPU util > 82% for 3m AND tail latency > 95th baseline.
2) Preflight: evaluate warm_pool and preemptible availability via capacity API.
3) Policy decision: if spare >= failover_margin -> start staged routing shift (10% every 30s). Else if preemptible available -> trigger borrow with spot fallback (notify finance). Else -> trigger emergency throttles and enable degraded mode.
4) Execution: incrementally shift traffic; monitor error budget and token burn. Keep route-level TTLs short.
5) Postmortem: tag incident with reserve_shortfall reason and timestamp; schedule capacity replenishment ticket.

Operational runbook snippets (to copy into SRE playbooks):
- Quick query: SELECT sum(provisioned_gpus) FROM region WHERE tag=reserved AND status=warm;
- Emergency borrow command: infractl borrow --region <r> --gpus <n> --type preemptible --ttl 2h

Outstanding questions / decisions: (bullet list for PM/Finance)
- Tolerable annual spend on idle reserved GPUs for enterprise SLAs? (propose 12% of fleet baseline)
- Acceptable preemptible mix rate by customer tier (free vs paid customers)?
- Do we formalize cross-region SLA latency budgets tied to reserve levels?

Action items (owners):
- Priya: wire up Monte Carlo constraints into capacity model (JIRA INFRA-1824) - due 2026-12-10.
- Marco: validate preemptible availability curves across cloud vendors - due 2026-12-07.
- Evelyn: draft finance memo with cost-per-hour reserve vs borrow scenarios - due 2026-12-09.

Quick links and references:
- Related maps: /shared_drives/engineering/infrastructure/cross-region-fallback-safety-margin-scenarios-aug-2026.json
- Simulation engine: https://git.company.internal/infra/capacity-sim (see branch reserve-policy-experiments)

Notes to reviewers:
This is exploratory. Prioritize feedback on (1) the conservative reserve pct per region, (2) the borrow window and TTL for preemptible use, (3) detection triggers for automatic failover. If we converge, convert to a formal spreadsheet with hourly simulation outputs and attach to the Dedicated contracts playbook.
